rows.sub: Between the tenth and the nineteenth centuries, Vietnamese rulers fought Chinese armies again and again. In many periods, they also sent tribute to the Chinese court.
rows.say: Between the tenth and the nineteenth centuries, Vietnamese rulers fought Chinese armies again and again. In many periods, they also sent tribute to the Chinese court.

rows.sub: At home, some Vietnamese rulers sat on a dragon throne and called themselves emperor. In letters to China, the same rulers accepted the title of king.
rows.say: At home, some Vietnamese rulers sat on a dragon throne and called themselves emperor. In letters to China, the same rulers accepted the title of king.

rows.sub: One recent study calls this emperor at home, king abroad. How did both fit together?
rows.say: One recent study calls this emperor at home, king abroad. How did both fit together?

rows.sub: The story starts in 939, when Ngô Quyền made himself king after defeating a Southern Han fleet.
rows.say: The story starts in nine thirty-nine, when Ngoh Kwee-en made himself king after defeating a Southern Han fleet.

rows.sub: In 968, Đinh Bộ Lĩnh went further. He declared himself emperor of a state called Đại Cồ Việt.
rows.say: In nine sixty-eight, Ding Boh Ling went further. He declared himself emperor of a state called Dye Caw Vee-et.

rows.sub: Yet he also sought recognition from the Song dynasty in China, and the Song gave him the title of a king.
rows.say: Yet he also sought recognition from the Song dynasty in China, and the Song gave him the title of a king.

rows.sub: In 981, the Song invaded. Lê Hoàn, the new ruler, drove them back. Within a few years, envoys were travelling again, and the Song granted him titles too.
rows.say: In nine eighty-one, the Song invaded. Leh Hwahn, the new ruler, drove them back. Within a few years, envoys were travelling again, and the Song granted him titles too.

rows.sub: The Lý dynasty kept the pattern. At home, its rulers were emperors. The Song granted them titles, including Prince of Jiaozhi and, later, King of Annam.
rows.say: The Lee dynasty kept the pattern. At home, its rulers were emperors. The Song granted them titles, including Prince of Jee-ow-jir and, later, King of Ah-nahm.

rows.sub: The pattern held even through war. In 1075, a Lý army under Lý Thường Kiệt struck first, taking towns in southern China, including today's Nanning.
rows.say: The pattern held even through war. In ten seventy-five, a Lee army under Lee Too-ung Kee-et struck first, taking towns in southern China, including today's Nanning.

rows.sub: A Song army struck back and was stopped at the Như Nguyệt river in 1077. Disease hit the Song camp, and both sides pulled back.
rows.say: A Song army struck back and was stopped at the Nyuh Ngwee-et river in ten seventy-seven. Disease hit the Song camp, and both sides pulled back.

rows.sub: How many fought? The accounts give very different figures. By 1084, the two courts had settled the border.
rows.say: How many fought? The accounts give very different figures. By ten eighty-four, the two courts had settled the border.

rows.sub: So what was tribute, exactly? In the 1940s, the historian John Fairbank described a "tribute system", with China at the center and smaller kingdoms around it.
rows.say: So what was tribute, exactly? In the nineteen forties, the historian John Fairbank described a "tribute system", with China at the center and smaller kingdoms around it.

rows.sub: Korea, the Ryukyu kingdom and Vietnam all sent missions, each on terms set by the Chinese court.
rows.say: Korea, the Ree-oo-kyoo kingdom and Vietnam all sent missions, each on terms set by the Chinese court.

rows.sub: A Vietnamese mission travelled overland, through the border passes near Lạng Sơn, then north through southern China to the capital.
rows.say: A Vietnamese mission travelled overland, through the border passes near Lahng Sun, then north through southern China to the capital.

rows.sub: The Chinese court could confirm a ruler with a title and a seal. Missions also carried gifts and formal letters.
rows.say: The Chinese court could confirm a ruler with a title and a seal. Missions also carried gifts and formal letters.

rows.sub: Some tributary states also used the Chinese calendar.
rows.say: Some tributary states also used the Chinese calendar.

rows.sub: Under the Ming, missions could also provide opportunities for trade, and receive return gifts.
rows.say: Under the Ming, missions could also provide opportunities for trade, and receive return gifts.

rows.sub: Historians still argue about what it all meant. Political scientist David Kang argues that this hierarchy helped keep East Asia relatively stable for centuries.
rows.say: Historians still argue about what it all meant. Political scientist David Kang argues that this hierarchy helped keep East Asia relatively stable for centuries.

rows.sub: Critics say that is too neat. Historian Peter Perdue argues the "tribute system" turned a flexible practice into a rigid model, and historian Prasenjit Duara has criticized aspects of Kang's account.
rows.say: Critics say that is too neat. Historian Peter Perdue argues the "tribute system" turned a flexible practice into a rigid model, and historian Pra-sen-jit Doo-ah-ra has criticized aspects of Kang's account.

rows.sub: Much of this lived on paper. The same court wrote two kinds of documents.
rows.say: Much of this lived on paper. The same court wrote two kinds of documents.

rows.sub: At home, edicts came from an emperor. In letters to China, the ruler wrote as a king, using the titles the Chinese court had granted.
rows.say: At home, edicts came from an emperor. In letters to China, the ruler wrote as a king, using the titles the Chinese court had granted.

rows.sub: One famous poem shows the home side. Tradition says it was read to Lý soldiers at the Như Nguyệt river. Its first line says that the southern emperor dwells in the southern land.
rows.say: One famous poem shows the home side. Tradition says it was read to Lee soldiers at the Nyuh Ngwee-et river. Its first line says that the southern emperor dwells in the southern land.

rows.sub: But the story of the poem comes from texts written centuries later, and historians such as Keith Taylor doubt that soldiers heard it in the form we have today.
rows.say: But the story of the poem comes from texts written centuries later, and historians such as Keith Taylor doubt that soldiers heard it in the form we have today.

rows.sub: Either way, the two kinds of documents sat side by side: a king in letters to China, an emperor at home.
rows.say: Either way, the two kinds of documents sat side by side: a king in letters to China, an emperor at home.

rows.sub: The system did not always keep the peace.
rows.say: The system did not always keep the peace.

rows.sub: After the Mongols first attacked in 1258, the Trần court agreed to send tribute. But Kublai Khan wanted more. He demanded that the Trần king come to his court in person.
rows.say: After the Mongols first attacked in twelve fifty-eight, the Chun court agreed to send tribute. But Kublai Khan wanted more. He demanded that the Chun king come to his court in person.

rows.sub: The Trần kings sent envoys and gifts, but did not go. War followed in the 1280s.
rows.say: The Chun kings sent envoys and gifts, but did not go. War followed in the twelve eighties.

rows.sub: After the fighting ended in 1288, Đại Việt went back to tribute. Sources say it sent a golden statue in place of the king himself.
rows.say: After the fighting ended in twelve eighty-eight, Dye Vee-et went back to tribute. Sources say it sent a golden statue in place of the king himself.

rows.sub: The Yuan were still discussing another campaign in 1293. But after Kublai's death in 1294, no new invasion came.
rows.say: The Yuan were still discussing another campaign in twelve ninety-three. But after Kublai's death in twelve ninety-four, no new invasion came.

rows.sub: A century later, the Ming invoked the restoration of the Trần as a reason to intervene. In 1400, Hồ Quý Ly had taken the throne from the Trần.
rows.say: A century later, the Ming invoked the restoration of the Chun as a reason to intervene. In fourteen hundred, Hoh Kwee Lee had taken the throne from the Chun.

rows.sub: The Ming emperor demanded the Trần be restored. In 1406, a Ming escort bringing a man who claimed to be a Trần prince was ambushed near the border, and he was killed. Chinese and Vietnamese sources tell this story differently.
rows.say: The Ming emperor demanded the Chun be restored. In fourteen oh six, a Ming escort bringing a man who claimed to be a Chun prince was ambushed near the border, and he was killed. Chinese and Vietnamese sources tell this story differently.

rows.sub: In 1407, the Ming conquered the country and made it a Chinese province again, called Jiaozhi. A Ming general wrote that they had recovered their ancient territory.
rows.say: In fourteen oh seven, the Ming conquered the country and made it a Chinese province again, called Jee-ow-jir. A Ming general wrote that they had recovered their ancient territory.

rows.sub: After twenty years of war, Lê Lợi drove the Ming out and declared himself emperor in 1428.
rows.say: After twenty years of war, Leh Loy drove the Ming out and declared himself emperor in fourteen twenty-eight.

rows.sub: Yet his letters to the Ming presented him as a loyal tributary. By 1431, the Ming had accepted him as ruler. The old pattern was back.
rows.say: Yet his letters to the Ming presented him as a loyal tributary. By fourteen thirty-one, the Ming had accepted him as ruler. The old pattern was back.

rows.sub: It could also be humiliating. In 1540, under threat of Ming intervention, Mạc Đăng Dung, who had seized the throne, submitted, ceded territory, and accepted a status below king.
rows.say: It could also be humiliating. In fifteen forty, under threat of Ming intervention, Mahk Dahng Zoong, who had seized the throne, submitted, ceded territory, and accepted a status below king.

rows.sub: The people who made the system work were the envoys.
rows.say: The people who made the system work were the envoys.

rows.sub: They were scholars, trained in literary Chinese, the shared written language of the region.
rows.say: They were scholars, trained in literary Chinese, the shared written language of the region.

rows.sub: In Beijing, they met envoys from other kingdoms. They could communicate in writing, with brush and paper.
rows.say: In Beijing, they met envoys from other kingdoms. They could communicate in writing, with brush and paper.

rows.sub: In 1597, the Vietnamese envoy Phùng Khắc Khoan, in Beijing to seek Ming recognition for the Lê king, met the Korean envoy Yi Su-gwang. The two exchanged poems.
rows.say: In fifteen ninety-seven, the Vietnamese envoy Foong Khahk Kwahn, in Beijing to seek Ming recognition for the Leh king, met the Korean envoy Yee Soo-gwahng. The two exchanged poems.

rows.sub: Yi Su-gwang's Korean record says only one member of the Vietnamese delegation could speak Chinese.
rows.say: Yee Soo-gwahng's Korean record says only one member of the Vietnamese delegation could speak Chinese.

rows.sub: In 1760, the scholar Lê Quý Đôn went on a mission to China.
rows.say: In seventeen sixty, the scholar Leh Kwee Doan went on a mission to China.

rows.sub: Historian Liam Kelley has studied their envoy poems, and how Vietnamese scholars pictured their kingdom within a shared classical world.
rows.say: Historian Liam Kelley has studied their envoy poems, and how Vietnamese scholars pictured their kingdom within a shared classical world.

rows.sub: Even after the biggest wars, the first step was often to ask for recognition.
rows.say: Even after the biggest wars, the first step was often to ask for recognition.

rows.sub: In 1789, after the Qing army retreated from Thăng Long, the Qing recognized Quang Trung as King of Annam.
rows.say: In seventeen eighty-nine, after the Qing army retreated from Tahng Long, the Qing recognized Kwahng Chung as King of Ah-nahm.

rows.sub: Sources say a stand-in attended the Qianlong emperor's birthday celebration in 1790.
rows.say: Sources say a stand-in attended the Chyen-loong emperor's birthday celebration in seventeen ninety.

rows.sub: In 1802, the new Nguyễn ruler, Gia Long, asked the Qing to recognize his country as Nam Việt.
rows.say: In eighteen oh two, the new Nwin ruler, Zah Long, asked the Qing to recognize his country as Nahm Vee-et.

rows.sub: The Qing court rejected the proposed name Nam Việt. In 1804, the Jiaqing emperor approved the name Việt Nam.
rows.say: The Qing court rejected the proposed name Nahm Vee-et. In eighteen oh four, the Jee-ah-ching emperor approved the name Vee-et Nahm.

rows.sub: At home, the Nguyễn court used other names too. In the late 1830s, it renamed the country Đại Nam, the Great South.
rows.say: At home, the Nwin court used other names too. In the late 1830s, it renamed the country Dye Nahm, the Great South.

rows.sub: French expansion brought the system to an end.
rows.say: French expansion brought the system to an end.

rows.sub: In June 1884, a treaty signed at Huế confirmed French control over Annam and Tonkin, central and northern Vietnam.
rows.say: In June eighteen eighty-four, a treaty signed at Hway confirmed French control over Ah-nahm and Tong-kin, central and northern Vietnam.

rows.sub: At the signing, the Vietnamese court was made to melt down the seal that the Chinese emperor had given Gia Long, in front of the French and Vietnamese envoys.
rows.say: At the signing, the Vietnamese court was made to melt down the seal that the Chinese emperor had given Zah Long, in front of the French and Vietnamese envoys.

rows.sub: China and France went to war in the struggle over Vietnam. In June 1885, the Treaty of Tianjin recognized the French protectorate, effectively ending China's claim to suzerainty.
rows.say: China and France went to war in the struggle over Vietnam. In June eighteen eighty-five, the Treaty of Tee-en-jin recognized the French protectorate, effectively ending China's claim to suzerainty.

rows.sub: The long run of envoys, seals and double titles, from the tenth century to 1885, was over.
rows.say: The long run of envoys, seals and double titles, from the tenth century to eighteen eighty-five, was over.

rows.sub: So was it submission, or a practical fiction? Chinese court records could describe a vassal. At home, Vietnamese court documents used imperial titles. Historians still weigh both readings.
rows.say: So was it submission, or a practical fiction? Chinese court records could describe a vassal. At home, Vietnamese court documents used imperial titles. Historians still weigh both readings.

rows.sub: Political scientist Brantly Womack calls the relationship asymmetric. The stronger side could not simply dominate, so both sides had to manage it.
rows.say: Political scientist Brantly Womack calls the relationship asymmetric. The stronger side could not simply dominate, so both sides had to manage it.

rows.sub: Which reading convinces you? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires for more.
rows.say: Which reading convinces you? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires for more.
